noise_items.item: Maintainability — hoist repeated flag reads (cache `const bool caseInsensitive`) — PR #42006
noise_items.why_noise: Borderline micro-optimization/style nit. It is framed as an enforced convention with real PR evidence, so it narrowly passes the signal filter, but 'compute a flag predicate once per invocation' is a low-durability maintainability point close to a formatting nit and is the weakest entry in Important PR Comments.

map_gaps: Item filtering: Include/Exclude Files, Folders, and Subfolders checkboxes (PowerRenameFlags ExcludeFiles/ExcludeFolders/ExcludeSubfolders = 0x10/0x20/0x40, driven by IPowerRenameItem::IsItemVisible/ShouldRenameItem in PowerRenameItem.cpp) are a distinct user-facing capability not explicitly mapped — only folded implicitly into the generic 'Item model (path, depth, selection, flags)' row.

File-time source selection: user choice of Creation vs Modification vs Access time for date tokens (flags CreationTime/ModificationTime/AccessTime = 0x4000/0x8000/0x10000, GetTime/PutFileTime) is not surfaced in the feature→file map, despite date tokens being mapped.
Actual per-item rename execution helper lib/Renaming.cpp (DoRename) is unmapped; rename is attributed only to PowerRenameManager.cpp orchestration.
anchoring_risks: Several confident single-line fix claims (PowerRenameRegEx.cpp:585, Helpers.cpp:457, dllmain.cpp:178, PowerRenameManager.cpp:757-793). Spot-checked and currently accurate, but exact line numbers drift; the file+function anchor is the durable part and should be trusted over the line number.

'Normalize once, at the boundary' asserts SanitizeAndNormalize is the single matching-layer chokepoint; verified it is applied to search, replace, and source in PowerRenameRegEx.cpp, but preview/UI paths (ExplorerItemViewModel) should be confirmed rather than assumed covered by the single-file claim.
